tools.name: data_broker_check
tools.description: Checks whether a business is registered as a data broker in California, using the MORVS California Data Broker Register: the 2026, 2025 and 2024 registries filed with the California Privacy Protection Agency and the Attorney General's 2020-2023 list, keyed by website domain so a name change at the same domain reads as one history. Give a business name, a website domain or URL, or both; matching is by registrable domain or by normalised legal name, DBA or earlier filed name (case, punctuation and legal-suffix insensitive, exact after normalisation), and when several brokers match they are returned as separate candidates, never merged. Each match carries the broker's filings as filed: what it says it collects, whom it reports having sold or shared data to, the laws it says regulate it, its own consumer-request counts, its name history and its broker page. Registration is self-reported and California-only, so a non-match is not a finding that a business is not a data broker, is exempt from registration, or has never registered. Businesses only; queries shaped like a personal name are not run.

name.description: Business legal name, DBA or earlier filed name, e.g. Cision or Trans Union, or a website URL; 2-200 characters. Give name, domain or both.

domain.description: Website domain or URL, e.g. transunion.com or https://www.equifax.com/, reduced to its registrable domain; 2-200 characters.

tools.title: Check Data Broker Registration

tools.name: data_broker_diff
tools.description: Compares two files of the MORVS California Data Broker Register (the 2026, 2025 or 2024 CPPA registry, or the Attorney General's 2020-2023 list) under the register's published method: a registration in the earlier file whose normalised legal name has no registration in the later file is an apparent leaver; if its website domain does have a later registration it is counted as re-registered at the same domain, with the later names, otherwise as not re-registered under either name or domain; a later registration whose name and domain are both absent earlier is net new. Returns the counts and the named registrations in each group, plus the register's own published figures for consecutive files. A registration absent from a later file is not an exit, a merger or a finding: registration is self-reported and California-only, and a business may have stopped brokering, merged, changed domain or simply not filed.

year_a.description: One register file: 2026, 2025 or 2024 (CPPA registry) or 2020-2023 (Attorney General list). Order does not matter.

year_b.description: The other register file, different from year_a: 2026, 2025, 2024 or 2020-2023. The earlier file is reported as earlier.

tools.title: Compare Data Broker Registries

tools.name: forced_labor_company_check
tools.description: Checks a company or facility name against the MORVS U.S. Forced Labor Company Register: every organisation named on the DHS UFLPA Entity List or in a CBP withhold release order or finding, the Consolidated Screening List (Commerce, Treasury) rows that match one of those names exactly, and issuer relationships a US-listed company states in its own SEC filing. Matching is exact on the register's name key (case, accent, punctuation and legal-suffix insensitive) or on a source-stated or reviewed alias (DHS "also known as" / "formerly known as", CBP "a/k/a"); there is no fuzzy, family-name or transliteration match, and several matching entities are returned as separate candidates, never merged. Each match carries its direct records, one per source row, with the list's own action, status and date, the source URL, the row locator and the snapshot date; with include_related (default true) it also carries filing-stated issuer relationships, which never extend an action to a parent. UFLPA listing, a CBP order or finding, and an export-control or sanctions row are separate actions under separate laws, and a non-match is not a clearance finding. Organisations only; queries shaped like a personal name are not run.

name.description: Company or facility name or stated alias, e.g. Needle Craft Ltd or XPCC; case, punctuation and legal suffixes ignored, no partial match; 2-120 characters.

include_related.description: Include issuer relationships stated in SEC filings (parent or subsidiary); default true. A relationship never extends an action.

tools.title: Check Forced Labor Register Company

tools.name: forced_labor_source_compare
tools.description: Compares two sources of the MORVS U.S. Forced Labor Company Register: the DHS UFLPA Entity List (dhs), CBP withhold release orders and findings (cbp), and the Consolidated Screening List rows that exactly match a DHS or CBP name (csl). Returns the entity ids named in both sources under the register's reviewed name and alias joins, the ids in source_a with no reviewed match in source_b and the reverse, with counts, the register's own published overlap figures, the source rows behind each listed entity (source URL, row locator, snapshot date) and each source's snapshot date, in pages of up to 50 ids per list continued with next_cursor. Issuers linked only through a filing are never counted, so a parent never enters an overlap. The sources apply different laws; an entity with no reviewed match in the other source reads "No reviewed name or alias match in this source snapshot", which is not a clearance finding.

source_a.description: First source: dhs (UFLPA Entity List), cbp (CBP WROs and Findings) or csl (matched Consolidated Screening List rows).

source_b.description: Second source, different from source_a: dhs, cbp or csl. Lists are reported as a without b and b without a.

limit.description: Maximum entity ids per list on one page; default 50, max 50.

cursor.description: The next_cursor value from an earlier page with the same sources; omit for the first page.

tools.title: Compare Forced Labor Register Sources

tools.name: pfas_system_lookup
tools.description: Looks up public water systems in the MORVS PFAS Drinking-Water Register, built from EPA's final UCMR 5 monitoring file, the ECHO SDWA system file and the Federal Register. Give exactly one of pwsid (one system), zip (every system that reported serving that ZIP code; a service-area hint, not a confirmed supplier) or state (one state file, or TRIBAL), optionally with name to filter a state's systems by system name or city. Each match carries the PWSID, display name, state, city, ECHO population served, owner type and its label, activity status, the six derived flags, the 2024 limits whose comparison cutoff at least one sampling-location average meets, and for ZIP queries the match scope; the answer carries source dates, the status of each limit named and the register's caveats. UCMR 5 results are entry-point monitoring samples compared with the 2024 limits by EPA's Table 4 method, not compliance determinations or household tap results, and EPA's May 2026 rescission and deadline documents are proposals. A system whose name the register withholds is shown by PWSID and city.

pwsid.description: EPA public water system ID, 9 characters, e.g. IA9778054. Give exactly one of pwsid, zip or state.

zip.description: Five-digit ZIP code, e.g. 51101; returns every system that reported serving it (a service-area hint, not a confirmed supplier).

state.description: Two-letter state or territory code of a register state file, e.g. IA, or TRIBAL for EPA-implemented tribal systems.

name.description: Text to find in system names or cities within state, e.g. Sioux City; case and punctuation ignored. Requires state.

limit.description: Maximum systems for a state query, largest population first; default 25, max 100. ZIP queries list every candidate.

tools.title: Find PFAS Register Water Systems

tools.name: pfas_rule_impact
tools.description: Compares two rule scenarios in the MORVS PFAS Drinking-Water Register: 2024_as_published (EPA's six 2024 PFAS drinking-water limits, final and in force) and if_proposals_final (the PFOA and PFOS limits only, as they would stand if EPA's May 2026 proposals to rescind the PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA and Hazard Index limits became final; they are proposals, not final rules). Returns each rule record with its status label, the number of systems and the ECHO population served with at least one UCMR 5 sampling-location average at or above a scenario limit's comparison cutoff (EPA Table 4 method), the PWSIDs whose only such averages are against limits proposed for rescission, the largest matching systems by population up to limit, the register's published figures for comparison and the method version, optionally filtered by state file, owner type and minimum population. These are technical comparisons of monitoring averages, not compliance results (not_compliance: true).

scenario.description: 2024_as_published (all six 2024 limits) or if_proposals_final (PFOA and PFOS only, as if the May 2026 proposals became final).

state.description: Optional two-letter state file code, e.g. SC, or TRIBAL; unfiltered counts equal the register's per-state figures.

owner_type.description: Optional ECHO owner type: F federal, L local government, M public/private, N tribal, P private, S state.

min_population.description: Optional minimum ECHO population served, e.g. 10000.

limit.description: Maximum systems listed, largest population first; default 25, max 100. Counts always cover every matching system.

tools.title: Compare PFAS Rule Scenarios

tools.name: pfas_system_history
tools.description: Returns one public water system's full record in the MORVS PFAS Drinking-Water Register by PWSID: each sampling location (a hashed key) with its sample events, first and last dates and complete-set averages in ppt, per-chemical sample and detection counts with the highest single result, the Hazard Index, the six derived flags, the six 2024 rule records with each one's status history and whether this system's averages meet its comparison cutoff, the source file hashes and the register's caveats. Raw samples are not published. UCMR 5 results are entry-point monitoring, not compliance determinations or household tap results, and EPA's May 2026 rescission and deadline documents are proposals. A system whose name the register withholds is shown by PWSID and city.

pwsid.description: EPA public water system ID, 9 characters, e.g. IA9778054.

tools.title: Get PFAS Register System Record

tools.name: data_demand_source
tools.description: Returns one publisher's figures for one report in the MORVS Government Data Demand Register. Figures are that publisher's own counts for its own period and scope. Companies count differently. Never add or rank figures across companies. A missing figure means not reported, not zero. National-security figures remain bands. These aggregate counts cannot show whether any person's data was requested. Defaults to the latest complete report; optional filters select exact fact fields.

source.description: Publisher id in the register, e.g. google or verizon. Unknown ids return the valid list. Figures are each publisher's own counts for its own period and scope.

period.description: Exact report period: YYYY-H1, YYYY-H2, YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD_YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the latest complete report.

geo.description: Exact ISO alpha-2 country code or WORLD, NONUS or XX; omit for every geography.

series.description: Exact published series id; omit for every series. A missing figure means not reported, not zero.

process.description: Exact legal-process id; omit for every process. National-security figures remain bands.

measure.description: Exact measure id; omit for every measure. Counts with different units must not be added or ranked across publishers.

limit.description: Maximum facts returned after filters; default 50, allowed 1-200. Aggregate counts cannot show whether any person's data was requested.

tools.title: Get Publisher Data Demand Report

tools.name: data_demand_compare
tools.description: Shows the latest headline row reported by each publisher in the MORVS Government Data Demand Register, side by side with each figure's label. The figures are each publisher's own counts for its own period and scope. Companies count differently; never add or rank their figures across companies. A missing figure means not reported, not zero. National-security figures remain bands. Aggregate counts cannot show whether any person's data was requested. Optionally restrict to one sector.

sector.description: Optional sector: big_tech, platform, ai, carrier, cameras_devices or official. Publisher counts have different scopes; never add or rank them.

tools.title: Compare Data Demand Headlines

tools.name: plate_reader_decisions
tools.description: Finds official city and county automated license plate reader matters in the MORVS License Plate Reader Register. Returns selected published decision fields with complete recorded action timelines, source links, vendors named in titles, and dollar figures exactly as printed. Filter by state, jurisdiction, vendor, recorded motion outcome, subject, decisive-action year or title substring query. Outcome means only the motion as recorded. An approval is an authorization, not proof of a signed contract or installed camera. A failed motion does not mean a contract ended. Amounts are printed figures, often ceilings, never money spent. No row means no qualifying action was found in the checked sources and period; it is not proof that no ALPR use exists.

state.description: Optional two-letter USPS state code, e.g. TX. A state with no row means no qualifying action was found in sources checked.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction client slug or case-insensitive name substring; no row means no qualifying action was found in sources checked.

vendor.description: Exact vendor name from the register; a named vendor does not prove a signed contract or installed cameras.

disposition.description: Recorded motion outcome code. Approved means authorization; a motion that did not carry does not mean a contract ended.

subject.description: Register subject code from the matter title; it describes the topic, not the outcome.

year.description: Four-digit year of the decisive recorded action.

query.description: Case-insensitive title substring, at most 80 characters.

limit.description: Maximum decisions returned; default 25, allowed 1-100. Amounts are printed figures, often ceilings, not money spent.

tools.title: Find Plate Reader Decisions

tools.name: plate_reader_state_law
tools.description: Returns the MORVS License Plate Reader Register's full state-law research record for one US state or DC, including official law citations and URLs, checked date, verification status, retention and sharing provisions, exceptions and search limitations. A "none_found" or unverified status describes the sources checked; it does not prove that no applicable law exists. Verify the current official text before relying on a provision.

state.description: Required two-letter USPS state code. A none_found, not_verified card means not verified; it does not establish no law.

tools.title: Get Plate Reader State Law

tools.name: federal_file_search
tools.description: Searches the MORVS Federal Files Register of federal Privacy Act systems of records by system name, number or ID, with agency, recipient, record-category, status and exemption filters. Recipient tags or groups and record flags are pattern matches on the agency text and count at least those matches; recipient matches exclude standard agency boilerplate. DHS matches do not imply ICE; ICE has its own tag. A routine use is the agency statement that it MAY disclose records for a purpose; it does not show that a disclosure happened. An exemption claim may limit access or correction but does not decide a request. Missing systems are not proof no records are kept. Results default to active systems and include published source context.

query.description: System name or number substring, at most 100 characters. A missing system does not prove no records are kept.

agency.description: Agency code from the register index. DHS is a separate tag from ICE and does not imply ICE.

recipient.description: Recipient tag or group from the index. Tags are text matches, reported as at least; a routine use says MAY disclose, not that it did.

flag.description: Record flag from the index. Flags are text matches, reported as at least.

status.description: Published system status; defaults to active. Use all for every status, or select one other published status.

exempt.description: Filter systems that claim an exemption; a claim limits access but does not decide an individual request.

changed.description: Filter systems linked to changes after the compilation; their last full published text may be out of date.

limit.description: Maximum matching systems returned; default 20, allowed 1-50.

tools.title: Search Federal File Systems

tools.name: federal_file_system
tools.description: Returns one published federal system of records by exact Federal Files Register ID, with the agency's record description, routine-use text, exemption claim, source record and linked Federal Register notices. Standard agency boilerplate routine uses are omitted unless include_standard is true. A routine use is the agency statement that it MAY disclose; it is not evidence a disclosure occurred. A later notice may change a system without reprinting its full text, so check linked notices and effective dates. Recipient tags and record flags are text matches counted as at least; DHS does not imply ICE. Exemption claims may limit access or correction but do not decide an individual request. A missing ID does not establish that no records are kept.

id.description: Published system id, e.g. DHS:/ICE-009. A missing id does not prove the agency keeps no records.

include_standard.description: Include routine uses marked standard; default false. A routine use says MAY disclose, not that disclosure occurred.

tools.title: Get Federal File System

tools.name: lobbying_client
tools.description: Returns client timelines from the MORVS Influence Register using a published key or a case-insensitive name substring. The register includes only reports with an AI, surveillance or privacy match in a lobbying-activity section; it is not a client’s complete lobbying history. Amounts are whole-report figures across all issues, never spending on a topic. In-house expenses and outside-firm income are separate and must not be added; subcontract income is excluded. Null is not zero. Filings do not establish a client’s position on a bill or a policy outcome. Returns the retrieval date and the LDA source disclaimer. A missing client is not proof of no lobbying.

client.description: Required case-insensitive client name substring or published client key, at most 80 characters. A missing client is not proof of no lobbying.

tools.title: Get Lobbying Client Reports

tools.name: wiretap_orders
tools.description: Finds individual court-authorized wiretap orders as published in one annual US Courts Wiretap Report. Defaults to the latest report year; filters use the report year, court, state, jurisdiction, offense group and intercept type. A row was reported to the courts in that report year and may have ended earlier. Results and costs are per order as reported. The annual headline count undercounts that year because some orders are reported in later years. Related orders can share people, intercepts and arrests, so do not sum those fields across rows. Zero or blank means none reported, not that nothing happened. Flags identify missing prosecutor reports and implausible figures. A missing row is not proof that no surveillance occurred; the published order shards start in 2016.

report_year.description: Report year; defaults to the latest published year. Each row is an order reported in that year; late reports can raise later counts.

state.description: State name as printed in the register, for example TEXAS.

offense_group.description: Offense group label from the register, for example drugs.

type.description: Interception type code from the register lookups.

limit.description: Maximum order rows returned; default is set by the register, allowed 1-100. Never sum people or intercepts across orders.

tools.title: Find Reported Wiretap Orders

tools.name: national_security_surveillance
tools.description: Returns the published agency counts in the MORVS Surveillance Orders Register national-security source ledger. Optionally filter by exact series ID and period. Every fact retains the agency label, source, page, quote, method and any qualifier or disagreement. Section 702 targets, FISA orders, national-security letters and border device searches use different units, laws and periods; never add them or treat them as one trend. Section 702 target counts estimate non-US persons abroad; FBI query counting changed. These are aggregate published counts and cannot identify surveillance of a person.

series.description: Optional published series id. Series count different things under different laws and must never be added.

period.description: Optional exact published period for the selected series.

tools.title: Get National Security Figures

tools.name: judgment_fund_payments
tools.description: Searches Treasury bi-weekly Judgment Fund payment lines in one fiscal year of the MORVS Judgment Fund Register. Defaults to the latest published fiscal year, which may be incomplete. Filters by named organisation payee, Treasury responsible agency or MORVS agency group, and minimum known grouped amount. Returns separate source lines grouped by named payee, agency and report period; unnamed lines remain separate. Includes payee status, Treasury report links and source row numbers. Individuals are never named. A payment is not an admission of fault; a line is not a settlement, and split or identical lines remain separate payments. The bi-weekly and annual Treasury products are separate and must never be added.

fy.description: Fiscal year, default latest published. Treasury products are separate and are never added.

payee.description: Case-insensitive payee substring. Names for individual or otherwise unnamed payees are never returned.

agency.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against agency or agency group.

min_amount.description: Minimum known amount of a returned payee, agency and period group, in dollars.

limit.description: Maximum returned payment groups or lines, allowed 1-100. A line is not a settlement.

tools.title: Find Judgment Fund Payments

tools.name: judgment_fund_payee
tools.description: Finds named organisations by payee-name substring in the MORVS Judgment Fund Register. Returns up to 50 matches by published amount, with total match count, summed bi-weekly payment-line amount, line count, agency groups, Treasury citation descriptions, and first and last report periods. Only payees confirmed as organisations appear; individuals are never named. A payment is not an admission of fault, a line is not a settlement, and the separate annual and bi-weekly Treasury products must never be added.

payee.description: Required case-insensitive substring of a named payee. Individuals are never named.

tools.title: Find Named Judgment Fund Payees

tools.name: mdl_lookup
tools.description: Find a federal multidistrict litigation (MDL) in the MORVS Mass Lawsuit Register by MDL number, caption word, or company word appearing in the Panel caption. Returns the Panel caption, category, district, transfer date, pending and total actions, the last 12 monthly pending counts, and terminated entries when available. Actions are lawsuits, not people. Centralisation is not a finding on the merits. A falling pending count is not a settlement or payout. A missing match only means no matching MDL was found in the published register.

query.description: Required MDL number, caption word or company word as printed in the Panel caption, at most 80 characters.

status.description: Optional published MDL status; defaults to all statuses. Centralisation is not a finding.

category.description: Optional category assigned by the Panel, not a conclusion about the cases.

limit.description: Maximum MDLs returned; default 20, allowed 1-100. Actions are lawsuits, not people.

tools.title: Find Multidistrict Litigation

tools.name: forfeiture_agency
tools.description: Find DOJ equitable-sharing agencies in one state or territory by agency-name substring or ORI. Returns DOJ database status and sharing labels, matched DOJ payments by federal fiscal year, and the agency's ESAC certifications by its own fiscal year with DOJ and Treasury as separate money fields. DOJ payment years and agency certification years must never be added, subtracted or treated as a gap. A certified balance is not misconduct. DOJ does not publish why an agency has a Non-Compliant or Ineligible status. A payment, review or audit finding does not establish unlawful conduct. Controlled-equipment entries itemise purchases already in ESAC spending categories and must never be added again. A seizure is not a crime or conviction. The newest ESAC year is partial; older thin years are marked in the response. Agency names are DOJ's; officials and other people are never named.

state.description: Required two-letter state or territory code in the register index.

agency.description: Optional case-insensitive agency name substring or exact ORI, at most 80 characters.

tools.title: Find Forfeiture Money Agencies

tools.name: forfeiture_payments
tools.description: Search DOJ equitable-sharing payments to state, local and tribal agencies by federal fiscal year. Defaults to the latest published DOJ year. Filters by two-letter state, DOJ-printed recipient-name substring and minimum row amount. Returns DOJ cash, sale proceeds, total, original recipient name, match method and matched ORI when one exists. A DOJ-masked recipient stays masked; an unmatched row is still a payment. With no state filter, returns all state subtotals and a separate foreign-sharing table. Foreign sharing is never added to payments to domestic agencies. Agency ESAC certifications use each agency's own fiscal year and include Treasury sharing; never add or subtract them from these DOJ payments. A seizure is not a crime or conviction; a payment follows participation in a forfeiture, not a finding of unlawful conduct.

fy.description: DOJ federal fiscal year; defaults to the latest published year.

state.description: Optional two-letter state or territory code in the register index.

recipient.description: Optional case-insensitive recipient name substring. Masked agency names remain masked.

min_amount.description: Optional minimum DOJ payment amount in dollars.

tools.title: Find DOJ Forfeiture Payments

tools.name: self_driving_company
tools.description: Find reporting companies in the MORVS Self-Driving Crash Register by published name or slug. Returns separate ADS and ADAS company profiles, report and incident counts, severity, location, confidentiality index, investigations, recalls and California DMV permits. share_of_kind is a share of reports, not a crash rate. A DMV permit holder may be a different legal entity; the register notes that difference. Reports are each company’s own filings with NHTSA, not a finding, and say nothing about responsibility. The highest injury severity alleged says nothing about responsibility. ADS and Level 2 ADAS have different reporting requirements, are kept separate and are never added together; OTHER is never a crash count. Reports and crashes are different counts. Counts reflect fleet size and reporting rules; they are not rates, are never normalised by miles or fleet size, and are never a safety ranking. The third amended order changed reporting from June 16, 2025, so counts across that break are not directly comparable. A narrative marked as confidential business information is a claim, not an NHTSA decision. No people or narrative text are returned. NHTSA’s caveats are included verbatim.

company.description: Required case-insensitive company name or slug substring, at most 80 characters.

tools.title: Get Self-Driving Company Reports

tools.name: self_driving_reports
tools.description: Search NHTSA Standing General Order crash-report rows in the MORVS Self-Driving Crash Register. Requires ADS or Level 2 ADAS and can filter by company, state, alleged injury severity, crash month and the year NHTSA first received the report. Returns latest report versions with NHTSA CSV citations, not narrative text. No report has its own NHTSA web page. OTHER filings are never returned as crashes. Reports are each company’s own filings with NHTSA, not a finding, and say nothing about responsibility. The highest injury severity alleged says nothing about responsibility. ADS and Level 2 ADAS have different reporting requirements, are kept separate and are never added together; OTHER is never a crash count. Reports and crashes are different counts. Counts reflect fleet size and reporting rules; they are not rates, are never normalised by miles or fleet size, and are never a safety ranking. The third amended order changed reporting from June 16, 2025, so counts across that break are not directly comparable. A narrative marked as confidential business information is a claim, not an NHTSA decision. No people or narrative text are returned. NHTSA’s caveats are included verbatim.

kind.description: Required report kind: ADS or ADAS. These kinds are never added together.

company.description: Optional case-insensitive company name or slug substring.

year_received.description: Year NHTSA received the report, 2021-2026; defaults to the latest published year.

severity.description: Optional published severity code. It describes the highest injury severity alleged, not responsibility.

crash_month.description: Optional crash month in YYYY-MM format.

limit.description: Maximum crash report rows returned, allowed 1-100.

tools.title: Find Self-Driving Crash Reports

tools.name: nhtsa_automation_investigations
tools.description: Search MORVS-reviewed NHTSA automated-driving, Level 2 driver-assistance and SGO-compliance investigations. Returns NHTSA’s structured action fields, cited SGO report IDs and published lookup links; scope and reason are MORVS-reviewed classifications, not NHTSA findings. Optionally includes linked recall campaigns with potentially affected units as filed by the manufacturer. An opened investigation or a defect petition is not a finding. A recall’s potentially affected units are not a fleet census. No NHTSA summary text or personal names are returned. Reports are each company’s own filings with NHTSA, not a finding, and say nothing about responsibility. The highest injury severity alleged says nothing about responsibility. ADS and Level 2 ADAS have different reporting requirements, are kept separate and are never added together; OTHER is never a crash count. Reports and crashes are different counts. Counts reflect fleet size and reporting rules; they are not rates, are never normalised by miles or fleet size, and are never a safety ranking. The third amended order changed reporting from June 16, 2025, so counts across that break are not directly comparable. A narrative marked as confidential business information is a claim, not an NHTSA decision. No people or narrative text are returned. NHTSA’s caveats are included verbatim.

status.description: Optional investigation status: open or closed. Opening is not a finding.

company.description: Optional case-insensitive manufacturer or company substring.

include_recalls.description: Include related NHTSA recalls; defaults to true. Potentially affected units are as filed, not a fleet census.

tools.title: Find NHTSA Automation Investigations

tools.name: prediction_market_filings
tools.description: Search event-type CFTC product filings in the MORVS Prediction Market Register by exchange code/name, listed year, filing status, MORVS topic, CFTC stay remark or public title substring. The default year is the latest published listed-year shard. A Certified filing was self-certified by the exchange under CFTC rule 40.2; it was not approved by the CFTC. Approval Pending and Approved are a separate product-approval route. Filings are not markets, volume, users or odds. Dates are as listed by the CFTC and can be re-dated after a status change. Topics are MORVS classification. Titles that may name individuals are withheld and are never searched; use the CFTC ID link for the source record. A stay is not a finding of a violation.

exchange.description: Optional DCM code or case-insensitive exchange name substring.

year.description: CFTC listed year; defaults to the latest published filings shard. Listed dates can re-date.

stayed.description: If supplied, filter filings by whether a CFTC stay is recorded; a stay is not a finding.

q.description: Optional case-insensitive title substring, at most 80 characters; withheld titles are never searched.

tools.title: Find Prediction Market Filings

tools.name: prediction_market_exchange
tools.description: Find a CFTC designated contract market (DCM) or pending application by exchange code or name substring in the MORVS Prediction Market Register. Returns CFTC-listed status/date and fixed-phrase remark flags, filing counts by listed year/category/status, stay and withdrawal counts, approval-pending and perpetual-futures counts, code-map evidence and open federal comment periods. Pending means only pending; a stay is a CFTC remark, not a finding. Filing counts measure filing practice, not markets, trading, users or odds. Dates are as listed by the CFTC and may be re-dated.

exchange.description: Required DCM code or case-insensitive exchange name substring; a pending application is only pending.

tools.title: Get Prediction Market Exchange

tools.name: china_ai_filings
tools.description: Search the CAC public generative AI, deep-synthesis and algorithm lists by a Chinese or English substring in the listed service or algorithm name, filer legal name, curated filer English name, or CAC filing number. Registry defaults to all; province applies to generative AI rows with a CAC province field. A us_list=true filter uses confirmed tier A legal-entity crosswalks only; brand uses an exact filer legal-name allowlist. Returns the CAC number, name and filer as printed, a separately labelled own English name or MORVS translation when available, CAC notice, date and its date type. The CAC says completed filing (备案) or registered (登记); neither grants approval. Filings are neither distinct models nor distinct companies. A brand in a filer legal name does not establish ownership. No match does not establish that a service or company is absent from China.

q.description: Chinese or English service, algorithm, filer or filing-number substring, at most 80 characters.

registry.description: CAC registry: genai_filed, genai_registered, deep_synthesis or algorithm; defaults to all.

province.description: Optional province as published in the CAC register.

us_list.description: If true, return only tier A crosswalk matches to a US list.

brand.description: If true, return only brand-name matches; a brand in a legal name does not prove ownership.

tools.title: Find China AI Filings

tools.name: china_ai_us_lists
tools.description: Read the curated crosswalk from CAC filer legal names to the US Entity List and Treasury NS-CMIC list. Search by Chinese or English entity-name substring; tier defaults to A. Tier A has published evidence for a legal-entity match. Tier B is a possible match, not confirmed, and is outside headline counts. Each entry gives the list name, start date, evidence type and text, and matching CAC record IDs. The Entity List imposes export-licence requirements for specified items subject to the EAR; the NS-CMIC investment ban covers specified US-person purchases or sales of publicly traded securities. These are different restrictions, not generic sanctions. The separate US actions timeline includes the DHS DeepSeek order with Federal Register links. MORVS does not determine whether any CAC DeepSeek filer is the company named by DHS. Not being on either US list never means an entity is cleared.

tools.name: breach_notices
tools.description: Search the Washington, Delaware or California Attorney General breach-notice list by public notifying-organisation name and year (notice year for Washington and Delaware, reported year for California). Timing uses only the dates in each record: Washington and Delaware results label whether the interval is beyond that state's statutory window by the record's dates. The records do not show permitted delays, including law-enforcement requests, or any enforcement outcome; the timing flag is no legal finding. Never call a notice "late" or say an organisation "violated" the law. California has no discovery date, so no timing is computed. Resident counts are notices sent to residents, not unique people, and are never added across states; Delaware also reports the company's stated total affected separately. A notifying organisation may differ from the breached one. Names that may identify individuals are withheld, never returned or searchable. Absence from these three lists is no evidence that an organisation had no breach.

state.description: Required Attorney General notice list: WA, DE or CA.

organization.description: Optional case-insensitive public organization name substring, at most 80 characters; withheld names are never searched.

year.description: Optional year of the state record date: WA/DE notice date or CA reported date.

beyond_window.description: WA or DE only: beyond the statutory window by the record dates; the records do not show permitted delays.

tools.name: breach_notice_organization
tools.description: Find public notifying organisations by name substring in the Washington, Delaware and California Attorney General breach-notice lists. Returns notice IDs and counts separately for each state, plus any paired Washington and Delaware notices whose notice dates are within three days. When paired discovery dates differ, the two states' records carry different dates; neither date is declared correct. Withheld names are excluded from this index and never returned or searchable. A non-match in these three states' records never means no breach: list coverage, reporting thresholds and organisation names vary. The notifying organisation may differ from the breached one.

organization.description: Required case-insensitive public organization name substring, at most 80 characters; absence does not mean no breach.
